name: Sendinês (Mirandese meridional)
notes: Sendinês subdialect of Mirandese, spoken in Vila de Sendim (southern extreme of Terra de Miranda). It inherits the full Central Mirandese system (graphemes_base=mwl: apical ⟨s⟩ /s̺ z̺/ vs predorsal ⟨c,ç,z⟩ /s z/, ⟨x⟩ /ʃ/, ⟨j,g⟩ /ʒ/, ⟨ch⟩ /tʃ/, ⟨nh⟩ /ɲ/, nasal-vowel digraphs) and overrides only the two documented Sendinês deltas: (1) monophthongisation of the Leonese diphthongs ⟨iê/ie⟩ → [i] and ⟨uô/uo⟩ → [u] (tirra not tiêrra, curpo not cuôrpo): the Central [jɪ]/[ʊ] is reduced to [i]/[u]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §50, p. 219) gives "fierro / firro" and §58 (p. 226) gives "bọ̌no / buno", "olho / ulho". (2) The Latin initial L stays [l] where Central Mirandese has [ʎ] (lhado → lado, lhuç → [ˈlus]): §111 (p. 259), "O L inicial latino mudou-se normalmente no mirandês central ou normal em lh; no sendinês porém conservou-se". Medial ⟨lh⟩ stays [ʎ]: LdV gives Sendinês ulho (p. 226), so only a word-initial ⟨lh⟩ is [l] (positional entry). Disagreement: the Primeiro Aditamento à Convenção (February 2000), as secondary sources report it, has Sendinês depalatalise every ⟨lh⟩ (alá for alhá, lhobo → [ˈlobu]), and the mirandese_g2p row alhá → [ɐˈla] follows it. The mirandese_dict rows tagged Sendinês keep the medial [ʎ] (olho → [ˈoʎu], mulher → [muˈʎeɾ]). LdV does not say that the medial [ʎ] is lost, so the spec keeps it. The Aditamento also lets Sendinese writers spell word-initial ⟨l-⟩ (not ⟨lh-⟩). The unstressed vowel qualities are inherited from Central Mirandese, where they are grounded in Leite de Vasconcelos's description of Duas-Igrejas (unstressed ⟨o u⟩ = [u], unstressed and final ⟨e⟩ = [ɨ]). Whether Sendinês realises those unstressed vowels differently is not settled by any description reached so far, and the Sendinês gold sample is too small to decide it; the inherited Central values stand until a published source says otherwise. SENDINÊS -ien. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §50, p. 220, Obs. 1): "Quando porém o ĕ latino se torna nasal e final, o sendinês offerece íẽ (com accento tonico no i)", with quíẽ, cíẽ, bíẽ. The three words are word exceptions, [ˈkiɨ̃], [ˈsiɨ̃] and [ˈbiɨ̃], because the syllabifier counts ⟨ie⟩ as one syllable and so cannot place the stress on the i. The plain ẽ is a cover symbol for a reduced nasal vowel. The footnote on p. 220 reads: "É difficil distinguir se o ẽ é ẹ̌̃ ou ẽ̥, por ser atono; i. é, se temos quíẹ̌̃ ou quíẽ̥; por isso escrevi simplezmente ẽ", so the vowel is [ɪ̃] or [ɨ̃]. §11, Obs. 4 (p. 185) gives the same ending as "-íḙ̃ ou -íẽ̥ em kíḙ̃ ou kíẽ̥ (quem,—no sub-dialecto sendinês)", so the vowel is [ə̃] or [ɨ̃]. The one value that both pages give is the "e surdo" nasal ẽ̥ [ɨ̃], and the spec uses it. Neither page gives the mid [ẽ], which is LdV's stressed nasal e (p. 180). When the word is proclitic, the digraph reduces to ĩ (MWL_SENDIM_IEN_PROCLITIC). Central quien and bien are the diphthong ẹ̌ (quĩẹ̌̃ p. 220), which has no spelling difference from the Sendinês words. A written final ⟨ie⟩ is [i] (positional entry): §56 (p. 225) gives tìệ as "em sendinês ti" and frìệ as "em sendinês fri". The stress is on the i, as in central Mirandese (fazie → [fɐˈzi]). A written final ⟨ue⟩ is [u] (positional entry): §67 (p. 232) gives rü(g)a > "rùệ, e em send. ru", so rue → [ˈru]. The word exceptions tue, sue, ũa, ũas, algũa and algũas, and non, repeat the central values (see the notes of mwl). ENDING "on" is [ɐ̃w̃] (Vasconcelos 1900, vol. I, §110, footnote: "Em sendinês parece que se diz -ão, ex.: rõuquidão, satisfação, como em português"), and ENDING "ion" is [jɐ̃w̃] for the same reason (Vasconcelos 1900, §110). The footnote is hedged ("parece"), and it is the only statement of a Sendinês -on.

sandhi_rules.name: proclitic quien, cien, bien
sandhi_rules.notes: In Sendinês the stressed íẽ of quien, cien and bien reduces to ĩ when the word is proclitic. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §50, p. 220, Obs. 2): "Mas se quíẽ, cíẽ, bíẽ se tornam procliticos, o digrapho íẽ reduz-se a ĩ: quĩ foi, cĩ pessoas, bĩ feito". He writes the proclitic forms with no accent, so the output has no stress mark: bien feito → [bĩ ˈfejtu], quien foi → [kĩ ˈfoj]. The left context also takes [β], the onset that MWL_SPIRANT_B_ONSET gives bien after a vowel. A pause blocks the rule, so bien before a comma keeps [ˈbiɨ̃]. LIMIT: the spelling does not show which uses are proclitic, so the rule reduces the three words before any following word in the same phrase.

allophone_rules.notes: Sendinês has the high central nasal [ɨ̃] in unstressed word-final -en, where central Mirandese has the mid central [ə̃]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §77, p. 239): "A -em atono no fim de palavras corresponde em mirandês normal -ḙ̃ e em sendinês -ẽ̥", with amen → amẽ̥, amassem → amassẽ̥, têem → tenẽ̥, devem → debẽ̥, and "o send. ẽ̥ representa uma das phases intermedias entre -ent e -ḙ̃". The ring below marks the "e surdo" [ɨ] (§24, p. 201: "i. é, e surdo (= e̥) nasal").

stress.notes: Convenção Ortográfica da Língua Mirandesa (1999) accentuation, Portuguese-based: paroxytone default; written accent (acute or tilde) overrides. Oxytone-attracting endings reflect Mirandese orthography: consonant-final r/l/z/ç (rapaç, Pertual, falar) and the final nasals written with -n in the Asturleonese manner — -in (camin, Sendin), -un, and the systematically oxytone -on class from Latin -ōnem (naçon, coraçon, Associaçon). Unmarked -an/-en verb endings stay paroxytone as in Portuguese -am/-em. The ending -ie is oxytone: the stress falls on the i of the hiatus (fazie, tenie, Marie), which the Convenção writes with no accent (2.1.2.1, PDF p. 20: "As palavras como mie (pronome possessivo), tenie, tenerie, darie, (formas verbais), Marie, die, não são acentuadas"). del is a clitic: Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, p. 188) writes it dẹ̥l, with the "e surdo". Dialect mwl-x-sendim: no evidence of stress-pattern divergence from standard Mirandese; block copied from mwl (cliticless_words included, since stress is not inherited). Sendinês has [l] for an initial ⟨lh⟩ by its own positional entry and monophthongises ⟨ie⟩→[i]; quien, bien and cien are word exceptions with the stress on the i. The article l is a word exception that MWL_ARTICLE_L_VELAR velarises before a consonant.

mirandese_g2p.measured: The mirandese_g2p row holds 11 gold pairs, per=0.3258, per_ci_low=0.1641, per_ci_high=0.4824 (benchmarks/results.json). The 95% interval includes 0.25, so the row cannot be read as a failure. The parent mwl spec's own mirandese_g2p row draws on the same underlying source with 205 pairs and measures per=0.1317, well under the threshold; the 11-pair Sendim subset is too small to show whether it genuinely differs from that larger measurement or is simply noise (audit is OWN_ONLY and is not inherited from mwl).
